title: NEET (UG) 2023 · 7 May 2023 · Code E1
instr: NEET (UG) 2023 held on 7 May 2023, Test Booklet Code E1, with the final answer key published by the National Testing Agency (NTA) on 15 June 2023.

200 questions: Physics 1–50, Chemistry 51–100, Botany 101–150, Zoology 151–200. Each subject has Section A (35 compulsory questions) and Section B (15 questions, of which candidates had to attempt any 10). Each question has four options (1)–(4) with one correct answer.

Marking: +4 for a correct answer, −1 for a wrong answer, 0 if not answered. As in the exam, only the first 10 questions you answer in each Section B are marked, so the maximum is 720 marks (180 questions).
Q2 (Physics) was dropped by NTA, so everyone gets its 4 marks. For Q150 (Botany) the final key accepts option (1) or (3).
source: Questions: NEET (UG) 2023, Test Booklet Code E1. Answers: NTA final answer key published on 15 June 2023. Explanations: All in All Exam Practice.

questions.text: Let a wire be suspended from the ceiling (rigid support) and stretched by a weight $W$ attached at its free end. The longitudinal stress at any point of cross-sectional area $A$ of the wire is :
questions.sol:
The wire is light, so the tension is the same at every point and equals the weight $W$.
Longitudinal stress = force / area = $W/A$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The ratio of radius of gyration of a solid sphere of mass $M$ and radius $R$ about its own axis to the radius of gyration of the thin hollow sphere of same mass and radius about its axis is :
questions.sol:
Solid sphere: $I = \frac{2}{5}MR^2 = Mk_1^2$, so $k_1 = \sqrt{\frac{2}{5}}\,R$.
Thin hollow sphere: $I = \frac{2}{3}MR^2 = Mk_2^2$, so $k_2 = \sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}\,R$.
$\dfrac{k_1}{k_2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2/5}{2/3}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3}{5}}$, i.e. $\sqrt{3} : \sqrt{5}$. None of the options gives this ratio (3 : 5 is the ratio of the moments of inertia, i.e. of $k^2$).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.note: NTA dropped this question in the final key: the correct ratio is $\sqrt{3} : \sqrt{5}$, which is not among the options.

questions.text: The equivalent capacitance of the system shown in the following circuit is :
questions.sol:
The two $3\ \mu F$ capacitors in parallel give $6\ \mu F$.
This is in series with $3\ \mu F$: $C = \dfrac{3 \times 6}{3 + 6} = 2\ \mu F$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A football player is moving southward and suddenly turns eastward with the same speed to avoid an opponent. The force that acts on the player while turning is :
questions.sol:
The force is along the change in velocity: $\Delta\vec{v} = \vec{v}_{\text{east}} - \vec{v}_{\text{south}} = \vec{v}_{\text{east}} + \vec{v}_{\text{north}}$.
With equal magnitudes, this points north-east.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: If $\oint_s \vec{E}\cdot\vec{dS} = 0$ over a surface, then :
options: the number of flux lines entering the surface must be equal to the number of flux lines leaving it.
the magnitude of electric field on the surface is constant.
all the charges must necessarily be inside the surface.
the electric field inside the surface is necessarily uniform.
questions.sol: Zero net flux through a closed surface means the net charge enclosed is zero (Gauss's law). The field need not be constant or uniform; it only means that as many field lines leave the surface as enter it.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The potential energy of a long spring when stretched by 2 cm is U. If the spring is stretched by 8 cm, potential energy stored in it will be :
questions.sol:
$U = \frac{1}{2}kx^2$, so $U \propto x^2$.
Stretching 4 times as far (8 cm instead of 2 cm) gives $4^2 = 16$ times the energy: $16U$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: If the galvanometer $G$ does not show any deflection in the circuit shown, the value of $R$ is given by :
questions.sol:
With no current through $G$, the 2 V cell draws no current, so the potential difference across $R$ equals 2 V.
The 10 V cell drives a current $I = \dfrac{10}{400 + R}$ through $400\ \Omega$ and $R$ in series.
$\dfrac{10R}{400 + R} = 2 \Rightarrow 10R = 800 + 2R \Rightarrow R = 100\ \Omega$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A 12 V, 60 W lamp is connected to the secondary of a step down transformer, whose primary is connected to ac mains of 220 V. Assuming the transformer to be ideal, what is the current in the primary winding?
questions.sol:
For an ideal transformer the input power equals the output power: $V_pI_p = 60$ W.
$I_p = \dfrac{60}{220} \approx 0.27$ A.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A full wave rectifier circuit consists of two p-n junction diodes, a centre-tapped transformer, capacitor and a load resistance. Which of these components remove the ac ripple from the rectified output?
questions.sol: The capacitor connected across the load acts as a filter: it charges at the peaks and discharges slowly between them, smoothing out the ac ripple.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Light travels a distance $x$ in time $t_1$ in air and $10x$ in time $t_2$ in another denser medium. What is the critical angle for this medium?
questions.sol:
Speed in air $c = x/t_1$; speed in the medium $v = 10x/t_2$.
Refractive index $n = \dfrac{c}{v} = \dfrac{t_2}{10\,t_1}$.
$\sin C = \dfrac{1}{n} = \dfrac{10\,t_1}{t_2}$, so $C = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{10\,t_1}{t_2}\right)$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Resistance of a carbon resistor determined from colour codes is $(22000 \pm 5\%)\ \Omega$. The colour of third band must be :
questions.sol: $22000 = 22 \times 10^3$: the first two bands are red (2) and red (2), and the third band (multiplier $10^3$) is orange.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
$\textbf{Statement I :}$ Photovoltaic devices can convert optical radiation into electricity.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$ Zener diode is designed to operate under reverse bias in breakdown region.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textit{most appropriate}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.sol:
Statement I is correct: photovoltaic devices such as solar cells convert light into electrical energy.
Statement II is correct: a Zener diode is heavily doped and is used in reverse bias in the breakdown region (for example as a voltage regulator).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The magnetic energy stored in an inductor of inductance $4\ \mu H$ carrying a current of 2 A is :
questions.sol: $U = \frac{1}{2}LI^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 10^{-6} \times 2^2 = 8 \times 10^{-6}$ J $= 8\ \mu J$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The angular acceleration of a body, moving along the circumference of a circle, is :
options: along the radius, away from centre
along the radius towards the centre
along the tangent to its position
questions.sol: Angular velocity and angular acceleration are axial vectors: for motion in a circle both lie along the axis of rotation (perpendicular to the plane of the circle).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.text: A Carnot engine has an efficiency of 50% when its source is at a temperature 327° C. The temperature of the sink is :
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two bodies of mass $m$ and $9m$ are placed at a distance $R$. The gravitational potential on the line joining the bodies where the gravitational field equals zero, will be ($G$ = gravitational constant) :
questions.sol:
Let the field be zero at distance $x$ from $m$: $\dfrac{Gm}{x^2} = \dfrac{G(9m)}{(R - x)^2} \Rightarrow R - x = 3x \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{R}{4}$.
Potential there: $V = -\dfrac{Gm}{R/4} - \dfrac{9Gm}{3R/4} = -\dfrac{4Gm}{R} - \dfrac{12Gm}{R} = -\dfrac{16Gm}{R}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A vehicle travels half the distance with speed $\vartheta$ and the remaining distance with speed $2\vartheta$. Its average speed is:
questions.sol:
For two equal distances $d$: total time $= \dfrac{d}{\vartheta} + \dfrac{d}{2\vartheta} = \dfrac{3d}{2\vartheta}$.
Average speed $= \dfrac{2d}{3d/(2\vartheta)} = \dfrac{4\vartheta}{3}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The amount of energy required to form a soap bubble of radius 2 cm from a soap solution is nearly : (surface tension of soap solution = $0.03\ \text{N m}^{-1}$)
questions.sol:
A soap bubble has two surfaces, so the new surface area is $2 \times 4\pi r^2 = 8\pi(0.02)^2 = 1.005\times10^{-2}\ \text{m}^2$.
Energy $= S \times \Delta A = 0.03 \times 1.005\times10^{-2} \approx 3.01\times10^{-4}$ J.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The minimum wavelength of $X$-rays produced by an electron accelerated through a potential difference of $V$ volts is proportional to:
questions.sol: The cut-off $\lambda_{\min}$ is reached when the whole kinetic energy $eV$ of an electron goes into one photon: $\dfrac{hc}{\lambda_{\min}} = eV \Rightarrow \lambda_{\min} = \dfrac{hc}{eV} \propto \dfrac{1}{V}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text: The half life of a radioactive substance is 20 minutes. In how much time, the activity of substance drops to $\left(\dfrac{1}{16}\right)^{th}$ of its initial value?
questions.sol: $\dfrac{1}{16} = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^4$, so four half-lives are needed: $4 \times 20 = 80$ minutes.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A metal wire has mass $(0.4 \pm 0.002)$ g, radius $(0.3 \pm 0.001)$ mm and length $(5 \pm 0.02)$ cm. The maximum possible percentage error in the measurement of density will nearly be:
questions.sol:
$\rho = \dfrac{m}{\pi r^2 L}$, so $\dfrac{\Delta\rho}{\rho} = \dfrac{\Delta m}{m} + 2\dfrac{\Delta r}{r} + \dfrac{\Delta L}{L}$.
$= \dfrac{0.002}{0.4} + 2 \times \dfrac{0.001}{0.3} + \dfrac{0.02}{5} = 0.5\% + 0.67\% + 0.4\% \approx 1.6\%$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In a plane electromagnetic wave travelling in free space, the electric field component oscillates sinusoidally at a frequency of $2.0\times10^{10}$ Hz and amplitude $48\ \text{V m}^{-1}$. Then the amplitude of oscillating magnetic field is : (Speed of light in free space = $3 \times 10^8\ \text{m s}^{-1}$)
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The temperature of a gas is –50° C. To what temperature the gas should be heated so that the rms speed is increased by 3 times?
questions.sol:
$v_{\text{rms}} \propto \sqrt{T}$. “Increased by 3 times” means the speed rises by $3v$, to $4v$, so $T$ becomes $4^2 = 16$ times.
$T_1 = -50 + 273 = 223$ K, so $T_2 = 16 \times 223 = 3568$ K $= 3295$°C.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: An ac source is connected to a capacitor C. Due to decrease in its operating frequency :
questions.sol:
$X_C = \dfrac{1}{\omega C}$, so a lower frequency increases the reactance and decreases the current $I = V/X_C$.
The displacement current between the plates equals the conduction current in the wires, so it also decreases.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
For Young’s double slit experiment, two statements are given below:
$\textbf{Statement I :}$ If screen is moved away from the plane of slits, angular separation of the fringes remains constant.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$ If the monochromatic source is replaced by another monochromatic source of larger wavelength, the angular separation of fringes decreases.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textit{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
questions.sol:
The angular fringe separation is $\theta = \lambda/d$.
Statement I is true: $\theta$ does not depend on the slit-to-screen distance $D$.
Statement II is false: a larger $\lambda$ increases $\theta$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In hydrogen spectrum, the shortest wavelength in the Balmer series is $\lambda$. The shortest wavelength in the Bracket series is :
questions.sol:
The shortest $\lambda$ of a series is the series limit ($n_i \to \infty$): $\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = \dfrac{R}{n_f^2}$.
Balmer ($n_f = 2$): $\lambda = \dfrac{4}{R}$. Brackett ($n_f = 4$): $\lambda' = \dfrac{16}{R} = 4\lambda$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The work functions of Caesium (Cs), Potassium (K) and Sodium (Na) are 2.14 eV, 2.30 eV and 2.75 eV respectively. If incident electromagnetic radiation has an incident energy of 2.20 eV, which of these photosensitive surfaces may emit photoelectrons?
questions.sol: Photoemission needs the photon energy to be at least the work function. 2.20 eV exceeds only the work function of caesium (2.14 eV), so only Cs emits photoelectrons.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text: The errors in the measurement which arise due to unpredictable fluctuations in temperature and voltage supply are :
questions.sol: Errors that occur irregularly, from unpredictable changes in conditions such as temperature or supply voltage, are random errors.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In a series $LCR$ circuit, the inductance $L$ is 10 mH, capacitance $C$ is $1\ \mu F$ and resistance $R$ is $100\ \Omega$. The frequency at which resonance occurs is :
questions.sol: $\nu_0 = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}} = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{10^{-2} \times 10^{-6}}} = \dfrac{1}{2\pi \times 10^{-4}} \approx 1592$ Hz $\approx 1.59$ kHz.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The venturi-meter works on :
questions.sol: In a venturi-meter the speed of flow rises at the narrow throat and the pressure falls there; the flow rate is found from this pressure difference using Bernoulli’s principle.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The ratio of frequencies of fundamental harmonic produced by an open pipe to that of closed pipe having the same length is :
questions.sol:
Fundamental frequency of an open pipe: $\dfrac{v}{2L}$; of a closed pipe: $\dfrac{v}{4L}$.
Ratio $= \dfrac{v/2L}{v/4L} = 2 : 1$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: An electric dipole is placed at an angle of 30° with an electric field of intensity $2\times10^5\ \text{N C}^{-1}$. It experiences a torque equal to 4 N m. Calculate the magnitude of charge on the dipole, if the dipole length is 2 cm.
questions.sol:
$\tau = pE\sin\theta = q(2a)E\sin\theta$.
$4 = q \times 0.02 \times 2\times10^5 \times 0.5 = 2000\,q \Rightarrow q = 2\times10^{-3}$ C $= 2$ mC.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The magnitude and direction of the current in the following circuit is
questions.sol:
The two cells oppose each other, so the net emf is $10 - 5 = 5$ V, acting in the direction of the 10 V cell.
Total resistance $= 2 + 1 + 7 = 10\ \Omega$, so $I = 5/10 = 0.5$ A.
The larger (10 V) cell drives the current from $A$ to $B$ through $E$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The net magnetic flux through any closed surface is :
questions.sol: Gauss's law for magnetism: magnetic field lines form closed loops and there are no isolated magnetic poles, so as many lines leave any closed surface as enter it. The net flux is zero.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A bullet is fired from a gun at the speed of $280\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ in the direction 30° above the horizontal. The maximum height attained by the bullet is $\left(g = 9.8\ \text{m s}^{-2},\ \sin 30^\circ = 0.5\right)$ :
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two thin lenses are of same focal lengths ($f$), but one is convex and the other one is concave. When they are placed in contact with each other, the equivalent focal length of the combination will be :
questions.sol: $\dfrac{1}{F} = \dfrac{1}{f} + \dfrac{1}{-f} = 0$, so $F$ is infinite (the combination has zero power and behaves like a plane glass plate).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The net impedance of circuit (as shown in figure) will be :
questions.sol:
$\omega = 2\pi \times 50 = 100\pi$ rad/s.
$X_L = \omega L = 100\pi \times \dfrac{50\times10^{-3}}{\pi} = 5\ \Omega$; $X_C = \dfrac{1}{\omega C} = \dfrac{1}{100\pi \times \frac{10^{3}\times10^{-6}}{\pi}} = 10\ \Omega$.
$Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_C - X_L)^2} = \sqrt{100 + 25} = 5\sqrt{5}\ \Omega$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The $x$-$t$ graph of a particle performing simple harmonic motion is shown in the figure. The acceleration of the particle at $t = 2$ s is :
questions.sol:
From the graph, amplitude $A = 1$ m and period $T = 8$ s, so $\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{8} = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ rad/s and $x = \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{4}\right)$.
At $t = 2$ s, $x = 1$ m, so $a = -\omega^2 x = -\dfrac{\pi^2}{16}\ \text{m s}^{-2}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
An electric dipole is placed as shown in the figure.
The electric potential (in $10^2$ V) at point P due to the dipole is ($\epsilon_0$ = permittivity of free space and $\dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} = K$):
questions.sol:
P is 5 cm from the centre O, so it is $5 - 3 = 2$ cm from $+q$ and $5 + 3 = 8$ cm from $-q$.
$V = Kq\left(\dfrac{1}{0.02} - \dfrac{1}{0.08}\right) = Kq(50 - 12.5) = 37.5\,qK = \dfrac{3}{8}qK \times 10^2$ V.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A bullet from a gun is fired on a rectangular wooden block with velocity $u$. When bullet travels 24 cm through the block along its length horizontally, velocity of bullet becomes $\dfrac{u}{3}$. Then it further penetrates into the block in the same direction before coming to rest exactly at the other end of the block. The total length of the block is :
questions.sol:
With uniform retardation $a$: $\left(\dfrac{u}{3}\right)^2 = u^2 - 2a(24) \Rightarrow 2a = \dfrac{8u^2}{9 \times 24} = \dfrac{u^2}{27}$.
Further distance: $0 = \dfrac{u^2}{9} - 2a\,s \Rightarrow s = \dfrac{u^2/9}{u^2/27} = 3$ cm.
Total length $= 24 + 3 = 27$ cm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In the figure shown here, what is the equivalent focal length of the combination of lenses (Assume that all layers are thin)?
questions.sol:
The combination is a biconvex lens ($n_1 = 1.5$) between two plano-concave lenses ($n_2 = 1.6$), all of radius 20 cm, in contact.
Biconvex: $\dfrac{1}{f_1} = (1.5 - 1)\left(\dfrac{2}{20}\right) = \dfrac{1}{20}$. Each plano-concave: $\dfrac{1}{f_2} = (1.6 - 1)\left(-\dfrac{1}{20}\right) = -\dfrac{0.6}{20}$.
$\dfrac{1}{F} = \dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1.2}{20} = -\dfrac{1}{100}$, so $F = -100$ cm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: For the following logic circuit, the truth table is:
questions.sol:
Each input passes through a NOT gate, and the two outputs $\overline{A}$ and $\overline{B}$ feed a NAND gate.
$Y = \overline{\overline{A}\cdot\overline{B}} = A + B$ (De Morgan's theorem), the OR function: $Y = 0$ only when $A = B = 0$.
This is truth table (2).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A horizontal bridge is built across a river. A student standing on the bridge throws a small ball vertically upwards with a velocity $4\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. The ball strikes the water surface after 4 s. The height of bridge above water surface is (Take $g = 10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$) :
questions.sol:
Taking upwards as positive: $s = ut - \frac{1}{2}gt^2 = 4 \times 4 - \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 16 = 16 - 80 = -64$ m.
The ball ends 64 m below the point of projection, so the bridge is 64 m above the water.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: 10 resistors, each of resistance $R$ are connected in series to a battery of emf $E$ and negligible internal resistance. Then those are connected in parallel to the same battery, the current is increased $n$ times. The value of $n$ is :
questions.sol:
Series: $R_s = 10R$, current $\dfrac{E}{10R}$. Parallel: $R_p = \dfrac{R}{10}$, current $\dfrac{10E}{R}$.
$n = \dfrac{10E/R}{E/10R} = 100$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A wire carrying a current $I$ along the positive $x$-axis has length $L$. It is kept in a magnetic field $\vec{B} = (2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 4\hat{k})$ T. The magnitude of the magnetic force acting on the wire is :
questions.sol:
$\vec{F} = I\vec{L}\times\vec{B} = IL\,\hat{i}\times(2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 4\hat{k}) = IL(3\hat{k} + 4\hat{j})$.
$|\vec{F}| = IL\sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = 5\,IL$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A satellite is orbiting just above the surface of the earth with period $T$. If $d$ is the density of the earth and $G$ is the universal constant of gravitation, the quantity $\dfrac{3\pi}{Gd}$ represents :
questions.sol:
For an orbit just above the surface, $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{R^3}{GM}}$ with $M = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3 d$.
$T^2 = \dfrac{4\pi^2 R^3}{G \cdot \frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 d} = \dfrac{3\pi}{Gd}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Calculate the maximum acceleration of a moving car so that a body lying on the floor of the car remains stationary. The coefficient of static friction between the body and the floor is 0.15 ($g = 10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$).
questions.sol:
Static friction supplies the body's acceleration: $ma \le \mu_s mg$.
$a_{\max} = \mu_s g = 0.15 \times 10 = 1.5\ \text{m s}^{-2}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The resistance of platinum wire at 0°C is $2\Omega$ and $6.8\Omega$ at 80°C. The temperature coefficient of resistance of the wire is :
questions.sol: $R_t = R_0(1 + \alpha t) \Rightarrow \alpha = \dfrac{R_t - R_0}{R_0\,t} = \dfrac{6.8 - 2}{2 \times 80} = \dfrac{4.8}{160} = 3\times10^{-2}$ °C$^{-1}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The radius of inner most orbit of hydrogen atom is $5.3\times10^{-11}$ m. What is the radius of third allowed orbit of hydrogen atom?
questions.sol: Bohr radius $r_n = n^2 r_1$. For $n = 3$: $r_3 = 9 \times 0.53$ Å $= 4.77$ Å.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A very long conducting wire is bent in a semi-circular shape from $A$ to $B$ as shown in figure. The magnetic field at point $P$ for steady current configuration is given by :
options: $\dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4R}$ pointed away from the page
questions.sol:
P is the centre of the semicircle. Each straight part is a semi-infinite wire ending level with P, at distance $R$, and gives $\dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi R}$; by the right-hand rule both point into the page, giving $\dfrac{\mu_0 i}{2\pi R}$ into the page.
The semicircle carries the current anticlockwise as seen in the figure and gives $\dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4R}$ out of the page.
Net field $= \dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4R} - \dfrac{\mu_0 i}{2\pi R} = \dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4R}\left[1 - \dfrac{2}{\pi}\right]$, pointed away from the page.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Which of the following reactions will NOT give primary amine as the product?
questions.sol:
(1) Hoffmann bromamide degradation gives methanamine, $\mathrm{CH_3NH_2}$ (primary).
(2) Reduction of a nitrile gives ethanamine, $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2NH_2}$ (primary).
(3) Reduction of an isocyanide gives a secondary amine: $\mathrm{CH_3NC \rightarrow CH_3NHCH_3}$ ($N$-methylmethanamine).
(4) Reduction of an amide gives ethanamine (primary).
So reaction (3) does not give a primary amine.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Match $\textbf{List - I}$ with $\textbf{List - II}$ :
$\textbf{List - I}$$\textbf{List - II}$
A.CokeI.Carbon atoms are $\mathrm{sp^3}$ hybridised.
B.DiamondII.Used as a dry lubricant
C.FullereneIII.Used as a reducing agent
D.GraphiteIV.Cage like molecules
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: Coke is used as a reducing agent in metallurgy (A-III). In diamond every carbon is $\mathrm{sp^3}$ hybridised and bonded tetrahedrally (B-I). Fullerenes are cage-like molecules such as $\mathrm{C_{60}}$ (C-IV). Graphite has slippery layers and is used as a dry lubricant (D-II).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as $\textbf{Assertion A}$ and the other is labelled as $\textbf{Reason R}$ :
$\textbf{Assertion A :}$ Metallic sodium dissolves in liquid ammonia giving a deep blue solution, which is paramagnetic.
$\textbf{Reasons R :}$ The deep blue solution is due to the formation of amide.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.sol:
Sodium dissolves in liquid ammonia as $\mathrm{Na^+}$ and ammoniated electrons: $\mathrm{Na + (x+y)NH_3 \rightarrow [Na(NH_3)_x]^+ + [e(NH_3)_y]^-}$. The ammoniated electrons give the deep blue colour and make the solution paramagnetic, so A is true.
The blue colour is not due to amide (amide forms only slowly, and the solution then loses its colour), so R is false.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: In Lassaigne’s extract of an organic compound, both nitrogen and sulphur are present, which gives blood red colour with $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ due to the formation of -
questions.sol:
When both N and S are present, fusion with sodium gives sodium thiocyanate, $\mathrm{NaSCN}$. With $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ it forms the blood-red complex $\mathrm{[Fe(SCN)]^{2+}}$:
$\mathrm{Fe^{3+} + SCN^- \rightarrow [Fe(SCN)]^{2+}}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text: The conductivity of centimolar solution of KCl at 25°C is 0.0210 $\mathrm{ohm^{-1}\ cm^{-1}}$ and the resistance of the cell containing the solution at 25°C is 60 ohm. The value of cell constant is -
questions.sol: Conductivity $\kappa = \dfrac{G^*}{R}$, so the cell constant $G^* = \kappa R = 0.0210 \times 60 = 1.26\ \mathrm{cm^{-1}}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as $\textbf{Assertion A}$ and the other is labelled as $\textbf{Reason R}$ :
$\textbf{Assertion A :}$ A reaction can have zero activation energy.
$\textbf{Reasons R :}$ The minimum extra amount of energy absorbed by reactant molecules so that their energy becomes equal to threshold value, is called activation energy.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.sol:
R is the NCERT definition of activation energy, so R is true.
On the NCERT (collision theory) picture, reactant molecules must always gain some extra energy to reach the threshold energy and form the activated complex, so A is taken as false.
So A is false but R is true.

questions.note: Assertion A is debatable: some reactions (for example the recombination of free radicals) have practically zero activation energy, and some coaching keys marked option (2). The NTA final key gives option (4).

questions.text: Which one is an example of heterogenous catalysis?
options: Oxidation of sulphur dioxide into sulphur trioxide in the presence of oxides of nitrogen.
Hydrolysis of sugar catalysed by $\mathrm{H^+}$ ions.
Decomposition of ozone in presence of nitrogen monoxide.
Combination between dinitrogen and dihydrogen to form ammonia in the presence of finely divided iron.
questions.sol:
In heterogeneous catalysis the catalyst is in a different phase from the reactants.
In (1), (2) and (3) the catalyst and the reactants are in the same phase (gases or solution), so they are homogeneous.
In the Haber process (4), solid iron catalyses the reaction of gaseous $\mathrm{N_2}$ and $\mathrm{H_2}$, so it is heterogeneous catalysis.

$\textbf{Assertion A :}$ Helium is used to dilute oxygen in diving apparatus.
$\textbf{Reasons R :}$ Helium has high solubility in $\mathrm{O_2}$.

Both A and R are true and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

questions.text: A compound is formed by two elements A and B. The element B forms cubic close packed structure and atoms of A occupy 1/3 of tetrahedral voids. If the formula of the compound is $\mathrm{A_xB_y}$, then the value of x + y is in option
questions.sol:
Let there be $N$ atoms of B. A ccp lattice has $2N$ tetrahedral voids, and A occupies $\dfrac{1}{3} \times 2N = \dfrac{2N}{3}$ of them.
A : B $= \dfrac{2N}{3} : N = 2 : 3$, so the formula is $\mathrm{A_2B_3}$ and $x + y = 5$.

$\textbf{Statement II :}$ When nucleoside is linked to phosphorous acid at $5'$-position of sugar moiety, we get nucleotide.

questions.text: The $\textbf{correct}$ order of energies of molecular orbitals of $\mathrm{N_2}$ molecule, is :

For molecules up to $\mathrm{N_2}$, mixing of 2s and 2p orbitals raises $\sigma 2p_z$ above the $\pi 2p$ pair. So the order is
$\sigma 1s < \sigma^* 1s < \sigma 2s < \sigma^* 2s < (\pi 2p_x = \pi 2p_y) < \sigma 2p_z < (\pi^* 2p_x = \pi^* 2p_y) < \sigma^* 2p_z$, option (1).

questions.text: The number of $\sigma$ bonds, $\pi$ bonds and lone pair of electrons in pyridine, respectively are:
questions.sol:
Pyridine, $\mathrm{C_5H_5N}$, is a six-membered aromatic ring.
$\sigma$ bonds: 6 in the ring + 5 C–H = 11. $\pi$ bonds: 3 (alternating double bonds). The nitrogen has 1 lone pair.
So 11, 3, 1.

questions.text:
Intermolecular forces are forces of attraction and repulsion between interacting particles that will include :
A. dipole - dipole forces.
B. dipole - induced dipole forces.
C. hydrogen bonding.
D. covalent bonding.
E. dispersion forces.
Choose the $\textbf{most appropriate}$ answer from the options given below :
options: B, C, D, E are correct.
A, B, C, D are correct.
A, B, C, E are correct.
A, C, D, E are correct.
questions.sol:
Intermolecular forces act between molecules: dipole–dipole, dipole–induced dipole, dispersion (London) forces and hydrogen bonding.
A covalent bond holds atoms together within a molecule, so it is not an intermolecular force. So A, B, C and E.

questions.text:
Which of the following statements are $\textbf{NOT}$ correct?
A. Hydrogen is used to reduce heavy metal oxides to metals.
B. Heavy water is used to study reaction mechanism.
C. Hydrogen is used to make saturated fats from oils.
D. The H-H bond dissociation enthalpy is lowest as compared to a single bond between two atoms of any element.
E. Hydrogen reduces oxides of metals that are more active than iron.
Choose the $\textbf{most appropriate}$ answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
A, B and C are correct uses of hydrogen and heavy water.
D is wrong: the H–H bond dissociation enthalpy (435.9 kJ mol$^{-1}$) is the highest for a single bond between two atoms of any element.
E is wrong: hydrogen reduces oxides of metals that are less active than iron, not more active.
So D and E only.

questions.text: The element expected to form largest ion to achieve the nearest noble gas configuration is :
questions.sol:
The ions formed are $\mathrm{O^{2-}}$, $\mathrm{F^-}$, $\mathrm{N^{3-}}$ and $\mathrm{Na^+}$, all isoelectronic with neon (10 electrons).

questions.text:
Select the $\textbf{correct}$ statements from the following :
A. Atoms of all elements are composed of two fundamental particles.
B. The mass of the electron is $9.10939 \times 10^{-31}$ kg.
C. All the isotopes of a given element show same chemical properties.
D. Protons and electrons are collectively known as nucleons.
E. Dalton’s atomic theory, regarded the atom as an ultimate particle of matter.
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
A is wrong: atoms are made of three fundamental particles (electrons, protons and neutrons).
B is correct: $m_e = 9.10939 \times 10^{-31}$ kg.
C is correct: chemical properties depend on the number of electrons, which is the same for all isotopes.
D is wrong: protons and neutrons are the nucleons.
E is correct: Dalton treated the atom as the ultimate, indivisible particle of matter.
So B, C and E only.

questions.text: The stability of $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ is more than $\mathrm{Cu^+}$ salts in aqueous solution due to -
questions.sol: Forming $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ needs the extra second ionisation enthalpy, but the small, highly charged $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ ion has a much more negative hydration enthalpy ($\Delta_{hyd}H^\circ$), which more than makes up for it. So $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ is more stable in water because of its hydration energy.

questions.text: Which one of the following statements is $\textbf{correct}$?
options: The daily requirement of Mg and Ca in the human body is estimated to be 0.2 - 0.3 g.
All enzymes that utilise ATP in phosphate transfer require Ca as the cofactor.
The bone in human body is an inert and unchanging substance.
Mg plays roles in neuromuscular function and interneuronal transmission.

questions.text: Taking stability as the factor, which one of the following represents $\textbf{correct}$ relationship?

Down group 13 the inert pair effect makes the +1 state more stable than +3. For thallium the +1 state is the more stable, so $\mathrm{TlI > TlI_3}$ (and $\mathrm{TlCl > TlCl_3}$).
For aluminium the +3 state is clearly the stable one ($\mathrm{AlCl_3 > AlCl}$), so (3) is wrong and (1) is the reverse of the thallium trend. Thallium is the element where the +1 state clearly dominates, so option (4) is the correct relationship.

questions.text: Which amongst the following options is $\textbf{correct}$ graphical representation of Boyle’s Law?
questions.sol:
Boyle’s law: at constant temperature $PV = nRT$, so $P = nRT \times \dfrac{1}{V}$. A graph of $P$ against $\dfrac{1}{V}$ is a straight line through the origin with slope $nRT$, so the higher the temperature the steeper the line.
Graph (2) shows straight lines with $T_3$ steepest and $T_3 > T_2 > T_1$, which is correct.
(1) has the curves in the wrong order (the highest temperature should be farthest from the axes), (3) plots curves against $1/V$, and (4) is a plot against $T$ (Charles’s law type).

$\left[\mathrm{CaCO_3 \xrightarrow{1200\ K} CaO + CO_2}\right]$

increase by a factor of six.
increase by a factor of nine.
increase by a factor of three.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as $\textbf{Assertion A}$ and the other is labelled as $\textbf{Reason R}$ :
$\textbf{Assertion A :}$ In equation $\Delta_r\mathrm{G} = -\mathrm{nFE_{cell}}$, value of $\Delta_r\mathrm{G}$ depends on n.
$\textbf{Reasons R :}$ $\mathrm{E_{cell}}$ is an intensive property and $\Delta_r\mathrm{G}$ is an extensive property.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.sol:
A is true: $\Delta_r G$ is proportional to n, the number of electrons transferred in the reaction as written.
R is true, and it explains A: $\mathrm{E_{cell}}$ is intensive (it does not depend on how much reacts), whereas $\Delta_r G$ is extensive. Multiplying the intensive $\mathrm{E_{cell}}$ by n (and F) is what makes $\Delta_r G$ depend on the amount of reaction, as NCERT explains.
So both are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.note: Some coaching keys gave option (2); the NTA final key gives option (1), in line with NCERT, which links the dependence on n to $\Delta_r G$ being extensive while $\mathrm{E_{cell}}$ is intensive.

questions.text:
Which of the following statements are $\textbf{INCORRECT}$?
A. All the transition metals except scandium form MO oxides which are ionic.
B. The highest oxidation number corresponding to the group number in transition metal oxides is attained in $\mathrm{Sc_2O_3}$ to $\mathrm{Mn_2O_7}$.
C. Basic character increases from $\mathrm{V_2O_3}$ to $\mathrm{V_2O_4}$ to $\mathrm{V_2O_5}$.
D. $\mathrm{V_2O_4}$ dissolves in acids to give $\mathrm{VO_4^{3-}}$ salts.
E. CrO is basic but $\mathrm{Cr_2O_3}$ is amphoteric.
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
A, B and E are correct statements from NCERT.

questions.text: Which complex compound is most stable?
questions.sol:
Chelating ligands form rings with the metal and give much more stable complexes than similar monodentate ligands (the chelate effect).
Only $\mathrm{[CoCl_2(en)_2]NO_3}$ contains a chelating ligand (ethane-1,2-diamine, bidentate), so it is the most stable.

questions.text:
Consider the following compounds/species:
The number of compounds/species which obey Huckel’s rule is ______.
questions.sol:
Hückel’s rule: a planar, cyclic, fully conjugated system with $(4n + 2)\ \pi$ electrons.
i. naphthalene, 10 $\pi$: yes. ii. cyclopentadienyl anion, 6 $\pi$: yes. iii. cyclobutadiene, 4 $\pi$: no. iv. cyclopropenyl anion, 4 $\pi$: no. v. cyclopropenyl cation, 2 $\pi$: yes. vi. cyclooctatetraene, 8 $\pi$ (and not planar): no. vii. anthracene, 14 $\pi$: yes.
So 4 species obey the rule.

questions.text: What fraction of one edge centred octahedral void lies in one unit cell of fcc?
questions.sol:
An edge of a cubic unit cell is shared by four unit cells, so only $\dfrac{1}{4}$ of a void at an edge centre lies within one unit cell.
(This is why the 12 edge voids contribute $12 \times \dfrac{1}{4} = 3$, plus 1 at the body centre, giving 4 octahedral voids per fcc cell.)

questions.text: Which amongst the following options is the $\textbf{correct}$ relation between change in enthalpy and change in internal energy?
questions.sol: $H = U + pV$, so at constant pressure $\Delta H = \Delta U + p\Delta V$. For gases $p\Delta V = \Delta n_g RT$, giving $\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta n_g RT$.

questions.text:
On balancing the given redox reaction,
$\mathrm{a\,Cr_2O_7^{2-} + b\,SO_3^{2-}(aq) + c\,H^+(aq) \rightarrow 2a\,Cr^{3+}(aq) + b\,SO_4^{2-}(aq) + \dfrac{c}{2}\,H_2O(\ell)}$
the coefficients a, b and c are found to be, respectively -
questions.sol:
Each Cr goes from +6 to +3, so one $\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}}$ gains 6 electrons. Each S goes from +4 to +6, losing 2 electrons, so 3 $\mathrm{SO_3^{2-}}$ are needed.
$\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-} + 3SO_3^{2-} + 8H^+ \rightarrow 2Cr^{3+} + 3SO_4^{2-} + 4H_2O}$ (charge: $-2 - 6 + 8 = 0 = +6 - 6$).
So a = 1, b = 3, c = 8.

questions.text: The equilibrium concentrations of the species in the reaction $\mathrm{A + B \rightleftharpoons C + D}$ are 2, 3, 10 and 6 $\mathrm{mol\ L^{-1}}$, respectively at 300 K. $\Delta G^\circ$ for the reaction is (R = 2 cal / mol K)

questions.text: Which amongst the following will be most readily dehydrated under acidic conditions ?
questions.sol:
Acid-catalysed dehydration goes through a carbocation, so the alcohol giving the most stable carbocation reacts most readily.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
$\textbf{Statement I :}$ The nutrient deficient water bodies lead to eutrophication.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$ Eutrophication leads to decrease in the level of oxygen in the water bodies.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true.

Statement I is incorrect: eutrophication is caused by water bodies becoming rich in nutrients (such as phosphates and nitrates), not deficient in them.

Consider the following reaction :

questions.text: The reaction that does $\textbf{NOT}$ take place in a blast furnace between 900 K to 1500 K temperature range during extraction of iron is :
questions.sol:
In the blast furnace the reduction of $\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}$ to FeO by CO takes place in the cooler upper zone, at about 500–800 K.
In the 900–1500 K zone the reactions are $\mathrm{C + CO_2 \rightarrow 2CO}$ and $\mathrm{FeO + CO \rightarrow Fe + CO_2}$, and the limestone forms slag, $\mathrm{CaO + SiO_2 \rightarrow CaSiO_3}$.
So reaction (1) does not take place in that range.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : One is labelled as $\textbf{Assertion A}$ and the other is labelled as $\textbf{Reason R}$ :
$\textbf{Assertion A :}$ The first stage of gametophyte in the life cycle of moss is protonema stage.
$\textbf{Reason R :}$ Protonema develops directly from spores produced in capsule.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{most appropriate}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is not correct.
A is not correct but R is correct.
questions.sol:
In mosses the haploid spore, released from the capsule, germinates directly into the protonema: a creeping, green, branched, filamentous stage. This is the first stage of the gametophyte; the leafy stage develops later from lateral buds on the protonema.
So A is correct and R, by saying that the protonema arises straight from the spore, explains why it is the first stage.

questions.text: In angiosperm, the haploid, diploid and triploid structures of a fertilized embryo sac sequentially are :
options: Synergids, Primary endosperm nucleus and zygote
Antipodals, synergids, and primary endosperm nucleus
Synergids, Zygote and Primary endosperm nucleus
questions.sol:
After double fertilisation the embryo sac contains: synergids and antipodals (haploid, $n$), the zygote (egg + male gamete, diploid, $2n$) and the primary endosperm nucleus (two polar nuclei + male gamete, triploid, $3n$).
So the haploid, diploid and triploid structures are synergids, zygote and primary endosperm nucleus.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Movement and accumulation of ions across a membrane against their concentration gradient can be explained by
questions.sol:
Osmosis, facilitated diffusion and other passive transport only move substances down a concentration (or water potential) gradient.
Moving and accumulating ions against their concentration gradient needs energy (ATP) and carrier pumps, i.e. active transport.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Large, colourful, fragrant flowers with nectar are seen in :
questions.sol: Flowers pollinated by insects are generally large, colourful, fragrant and rich in nectar, which attract the insects. Wind-pollinated flowers are small and inconspicuous with no nectar or scent.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: The phenomenon of pleiotropism refers to
options: presence of several alleles of a single gene controlling a single crossover.
presence of two alleles, each of the two genes controlling a single trait.
a single gene affecting multiple phenotypic expression.
more than two genes affecting a single character.
questions.sol:
In pleiotropy a single gene has more than one phenotypic effect (for example, the gene for phenylketonuria affects mental development as well as hair and skin pigmentation).
Several genes affecting one character is polygenic inheritance, not pleiotropy.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Which hormone promotes internode/petiole elongation in deep water rice?
questions.sol: Ethylene promotes rapid elongation of internodes and petioles in deep water rice plants, which keeps the leaves and upper parts of the shoot above the water.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Among ‘The Evil Quartet’, which one is considered the most important cause driving extinction of species?
questions.sol: The four major causes of biodiversity loss (the ‘Evil Quartet’) are habitat loss and fragmentation, over-exploitation, alien species invasions and co-extinctions. Habitat loss and fragmentation is the most important cause driving animals and plants to extinction.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Upon exposure to UV radiation, DNA stained with ethidium bromide will show
questions.sol: After gel electrophoresis, DNA fragments are stained with ethidium bromide and seen under ultraviolet light as bright orange coloured bands.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Which micronutrient is required for splitting of water molecule during photosynthesis?
questions.sol:
Manganese activates many enzymes and its best-defined role is in the splitting of water to liberate oxygen during photosynthesis (with PS II).
Magnesium is a macronutrient (part of chlorophyll); molybdenum is a component of nitrogenase and nitrate reductase.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Axile placentation is observed in
questions.sol:
In axile placentation the ovary is multilocular and the placenta is axial, as in china rose, tomato, lemon and petunia.
Mustard and cucumber have parietal, primrose and $\textit{Dianthus}$ free central, and pea, beans and lupin marginal placentation. So only option (4) is entirely axile.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: The process of appearance of recombination nodules occurs at which sub stage of prophase I in meiosis?
questions.sol: During pachytene the bivalents (tetrads) are clearly seen and recombination nodules appear: these are the sites where crossing over between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes takes place.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: The reaction centre in PS II has an absorption maxima at
questions.sol: The reaction centre chlorophyll $a$ of PS II absorbs maximally at 680 nm (P680); that of PS I absorbs at 700 nm (P700).
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Unequivocal proof that DNA is the genetic material was first proposed by
questions.sol: Griffith showed transformation, and Avery, MacLeod and McCarty identified DNA as the transforming principle. The unequivocal proof that DNA is the genetic material came from Hershey and Chase (1952), using bacteriophages labelled with radioactive phosphorus and sulphur.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Among eukaryotes, replication of DNA takes place in -
questions.sol: DNA replication takes place during the S (synthesis) phase of interphase, when the amount of DNA per cell doubles.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: In tissue culture experiments, leaf mesophyll cells are put in a culture medium to form callus. This phenomenon may be called as -
questions.sol: Mesophyll cells are already differentiated and have lost the ability to divide. When they regain the capacity to divide and form an undifferentiated mass (callus), the process is dedifferentiation.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Cellulose does not form blue colour with Iodine because
options: It does not contain complex helices and hence cannot hold iodine molecules.
It breakes down when iodine reacts with it.
questions.sol: Starch forms helical secondary structures that can hold iodine, giving a blue colour. Cellulose is a polymer of glucose with straight chains that do not form such complex helices, so it cannot hold iodine and gives no blue colour.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Spraying of which of the following phytohormone on juvenile conifers helps in hastening the maturity period, that leads to early seed production?
questions.sol: Gibberellins sprayed on juvenile conifers hasten the maturity period, which leads to early seed production.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
$\textbf{Statement I :}$ The forces generated by transpiration can lift a xylem-sized column of water over 130 meters height.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$ Transpiration cools leaf surfaces sometimes 10 to 15 degrees, by evaporative cooling.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{most appropriate}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.sol: Both are facts about transpiration: the transpiration pull can lift a xylem-sized column of water over 130 metres, and evaporation of water from the leaf cools its surface, sometimes by 10 to 15 degrees.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Family Fabaceae differs from Solanaceae and Liliaceae. With respect to the stamens, pick out the characteristics specific to family Fabaceae but not found in Solanaceae or Liliaceae.
questions.sol: Fabaceae: ten stamens, diadelphous (9 + 1), anthers dithecous. Solanaceae: five epipetalous stamens. Liliaceae: six epiphyllous (epitepalous) stamens. Dithecous anthers are also found in the other two families, but the diadelphous condition is specific to Fabaceae, so option (1) describes Fabaceae.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Expressed Sequence Tags (ESTs) refers to
options: All genes that are expressed as RNA.
All genes that are expressed as proteins.
All genes whether expressed or unexpressed.
questions.sol: In the Human Genome Project, one approach identified all the genes that are expressed as RNA; these are called Expressed Sequence Tags (ESTs). The other approach, sequence annotation, sequenced the whole genome, coding and non-coding.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Identify the $\textbf{correct}$ statements :
A. Detrivores perform fragmentation.
B. The humus is further degraded by some microbes during mineralization.
C. Water soluble inorganic nutrients go down into the soil and get precipitated by a process called leaching.
D. The detritus food chain begins with living organisms.
E. Earthworms break down detritus into smaller particles by a process called catabolism.
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
A, B and C are correct: detritivores such as earthworms carry out fragmentation; humus is slowly degraded by microbes, releasing inorganic nutrients (mineralisation); and water-soluble nutrients move down into the soil and are precipitated as unavailable salts (leaching).
D is wrong: the detritus food chain begins with dead organic matter. E is wrong: breaking detritus into smaller particles is fragmentation; catabolism is the enzymatic breakdown by bacteria and fungi.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: The thickness of ozone in a column of air in the atmosphere is measured in terms of :
questions.sol: The thickness of the ozone in a column of air from the ground to the top of the atmosphere is measured in Dobson units (DU). Decibels measure sound level and kilobase measures DNA length.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : One is labelled as $\textbf{Assertion A}$ and the other is labelled as $\textbf{Reason R}$ :
$\textbf{Assertion A :}$ Late wood has fewer xylary elements with narrow vessels.
$\textbf{Reason R :}$ Cambium is less active in winters.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.sol:
In winter the cambium is less active and forms fewer xylary elements with narrow vessels; this is late wood (autumn wood). In spring the cambium is very active and forms early wood with wide vessels.
So both are true and R explains A.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Which of the following stages of meiosis involves division of centromere?
questions.sol: In anaphase I the homologous chromosomes separate but the sister chromatids stay joined at their centromeres. In anaphase II the centromere of each chromosome splits, so the sister chromatids move to opposite poles.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: The historic Convention on Biological Diversity, ‘The Earth Summit’ was held in Rio de Janeiro in the year :
questions.sol: The Earth Summit (Convention on Biological Diversity) was held in Rio de Janeiro in 1992. The World Summit on Sustainable Development followed in Johannesburg in 2002.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: How many ATP and $\mathrm{NADPH_2}$ are required for the synthesis of one molecule of Glucose during Calvin cycle?
questions.sol: Fixing one $\mathrm{CO_2}$ in the Calvin cycle needs 3 ATP and 2 NADPH. One glucose needs six turns of the cycle: $6 \times 3 = 18$ ATP and $6 \times 2 = 12$ NADPH.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
In the equation
GPP − R = NPP
GPP is Gross Primary Productivity
NPP is Net Primary Productivity
R here is __________.
questions.sol: Net primary productivity is the gross primary productivity minus the energy used by the plants in respiration. So R is the respiratory loss.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: During the purification process for recombinant DNA technology, addition of chilled ethanol precipitates out
questions.sol: After the cell is broken open and RNA, proteins and other molecules are removed with enzymes (ribonuclease, protease), adding chilled ethanol makes the purified DNA precipitate out as a mass of fine threads.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: What is the role of RNA polymerase III in the process of transcription in Eukaryotes?
options: Transcription of tRNA, 5 srRNA and snRNA
questions.sol: In eukaryotes RNA polymerase I transcribes the 28S, 18S and 5.8S rRNAs; RNA polymerase II transcribes the precursor of mRNA (hnRNA); and RNA polymerase III transcribes tRNA, 5S rRNA and snRNAs.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: What is the function of tassels in the corn cob?
questions.sol: Maize is wind pollinated. The tassels of the corn cob are its stigmas and styles, which move in the wind and trap pollen grains.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Identify the pair of heterosporous pteridophytes among the following :
questions.sol: Most pteridophytes are homosporous ($\textit{Lycopodium}$, $\textit{Psilotum}$, $\textit{Equisetum}$). $\textit{Selaginella}$ and $\textit{Salvinia}$ produce two kinds of spores (macrospores and microspores), so they are heterosporous.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: In gene gun method used to introduce alien DNA into host cells, microparticles of __________ metal are used.
questions.sol: In biolistics (the gene gun), cells are bombarded with high-velocity microparticles of gold or tungsten coated with DNA.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
$\textbf{Statement I :}$ Endarch and exarch are the terms often used for describing the position of secondary xylem in the plant body.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$ Exarch condition is the most common feature of the root system.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true.
questions.sol:
Statement I is incorrect: endarch and exarch describe the position of the protoxylem in the primary xylem, not secondary xylem. In stems the protoxylem lies towards the centre (endarch).
Statement II is true: in roots the protoxylem lies towards the periphery (exarch).
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Frequency of recombination between gene pairs on same chromosome as a measure of the distance between genes to map their position on chromosome, was used for the first time by
questions.sol: Alfred Sturtevant, a student of Morgan, used the frequency of recombination between gene pairs on the same chromosome as a measure of the distance between them and so mapped their positions on the chromosome.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : One is labelled as $\textbf{Assertion A}$ and the other is labelled as $\textbf{Reason R}$ :
$\textbf{Assertion A :}$ ATP is used at two steps in glycolysis.
$\textbf{Reason R :}$ First ATP is used in converting glucose into glucose-6-phosphate and second ATP is used in conversion of fructose-6-phosphate into fructose-1-6-diphosphate.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.sol:
ATP is consumed at two steps of glycolysis: phosphorylation of glucose to glucose-6-phosphate (hexokinase) and of fructose-6-phosphate to fructose-1,6-bisphosphate (phosphofructokinase).
So both are true and R explains A.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Which one of the following statements is $\textbf{NOT}$ correct?
options: The micro-organisms involved in biodegradation of organic matter in a sewage polluted water body consume a lot of oxygen causing the death of aquatic organisms.
Algal blooms caused by excess of organic matter in water improve water quality and promote fisheries.
Water hyacinth grows abundantly in eutrophic water bodies and leads to an imbalance in the ecosystem dynamics of the water body.
The amount of some toxic substances of industrial waste water increases in the organisms at successive trophic levels.
questions.sol:
Algal blooms, caused by excess nutrients, deteriorate water quality: they colour the water, give off bad odours, use up dissolved oxygen and kill fish. So statement (2) is not correct.
(1) describes the high BOD of sewage-polluted water, (3) is true of water hyacinth in eutrophic water and (4) describes biomagnification.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: How many different proteins does the ribosome consist of?
questions.sol: The ribosome, the cellular factory for protein synthesis, consists of structural RNAs and about 80 different proteins.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Which of the following statements are correct about Klinefelter’s Syndrome?
A. This disorder was first described by Langdon Down (1866).
B. Such an individual has overall masculine development. However, the feminine development is also expressed.
C. The affected individual is short statured.
D. Physical, psychomotor and mental development is retarded.
E. Such individuals are sterile.
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Klinefelter’s syndrome (47, XXY) gives an individual with overall masculine development but some feminine features (such as gynaecomastia), and such individuals are sterile: B and E are correct.
A, C and D describe Down’s syndrome (described by Langdon Down in 1866): short stature and retarded physical, psychomotor and mental development.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Match List I with List II :
List IList II
A.Oxidative decarboxylationI.Citrate synthase
B.GlycolysisII.Pyruvate dehydrogenase
C.Oxidative phosphorylationIII.Electron transport system
D.Tricarboxylic acid cycleIV.EMP pathway
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: Oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvate to acetyl CoA is catalysed by pyruvate dehydrogenase (A-II). Glycolysis is the EMP pathway (B-IV). Oxidative phosphorylation is linked to the electron transport system (C-III). The TCA cycle begins with citrate synthase joining acetyl CoA and oxaloacetic acid (D-I).
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : One is labelled as $\textbf{Assertion A}$ and the other is labelled as $\textbf{Reason R}$ :
$\textbf{Assertion A :}$ A flower is defined as modified shoot wherein the shoot apical meristem changes to floral meristem.
$\textbf{Reason R :}$ Internode of the shoot gets condensed to produce different floral appendages laterally at successive nodes instead of leaves.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.sol:
A flower is a modified shoot: the shoot apical meristem changes into a floral meristem, the internodes do not elongate and the axis gets condensed, and at successive nodes floral appendages arise laterally instead of leaves.
So both are true and R explains A.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : One is labelled as $\textbf{Assertion A}$ and the other is labelled as $\textbf{Reason R}$ :
$\textbf{Assertion A :}$ In gymnosperms the pollen grains are released from the microsporangium and carried by air currents.
$\textbf{Reason R :}$ Air currents carry the pollen grains to the mouth of the archegonia where the male gametes are discharged and pollen tube is not formed.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.sol:
A is true: gymnosperm pollen grains are released from the microsporangia and carried by air currents to the opening of the ovules.
R is false: the pollen grain forms a pollen tube, which carries the male gametes towards the archegonia; the pollen is not carried to the mouth of the archegonia.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Match List I with List II :
List IList II
A.CohesionI.More attraction in liquid phase
B.AdhesionII.Mutual attraction among water molecules
C.Surface tensionIII.Water loss in liquid phase
D.GuttationIV.Attraction towards polar surfaces
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: Cohesion is the mutual attraction between water molecules (A-II). Adhesion is attraction of water to polar surfaces (B-IV). Surface tension arises because water molecules are more attracted to each other in the liquid phase than to water in the gas phase (C-I). Guttation is loss of water in liquid form from leaf margins (D-III).
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Which of the following combinations is required for chemiosmosis?
options: membrane, proton pump, proton gradient, ATP synthase
membrane, proton pump, proton gradient, NADP synthase
proton pump, electron gradient, ATP synthase
proton pump, electron gradient, NADP synthase
questions.sol: Chemiosmosis needs a membrane, a proton pump, a proton gradient across the membrane and ATP synthase: protons flowing back through the ATP synthase channel drive the synthesis of ATP.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Melonate inhibits the growth of pathogenic bacteria by inhibiting the activity of
questions.sol: Malonate closely resembles succinate in structure, so it acts as a competitive inhibitor of succinic dehydrogenase; such inhibitors are used to control bacterial pathogens.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Identify the $\textbf{correct}$ statements :
A. Lenticels are the lens-shaped openings permitting the exchange of gases.
B. Bark formed early in the season is called hard bark.
C. Bark is a technical term that refers to all tissues exterior to vascular cambium.
D. Bark refers to periderm and secondary phloem.
E. Phellogen is single-layered in thickness.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
A is correct: lenticels are lens-shaped openings for gaseous exchange. D is correct: bark includes the periderm and the secondary phloem.
B is wrong: bark formed early in the season is soft (early) bark. C is wrong: bark is a non-technical term. E is wrong: phellogen is a couple of layers thick.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Match List I with List II :
List IList II
A.M PhaseI.Proteins are synthesized
B.$\mathrm{G_2}$ PhaseII.Inactive phase
C.Quiescent stageIII.Interval between mitosis and initiation of DNA replication
D.$\mathrm{G_1}$ PhaseIV.Equational division
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: M phase is the phase of equational division, mitosis (A-IV). In $\mathrm{G_2}$ proteins are synthesised in preparation for mitosis (B-I). The quiescent stage ($\mathrm{G_0}$) is an inactive stage (C-II). $\mathrm{G_1}$ is the interval between mitosis and the start of DNA replication (D-III).
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Match List I with List II :
List I
(Interaction)		List II
(Species A and B)
A.MutualismI.+(A), O(B)
B.CommensalismII.−(A), O(B)
C.AmensalismIII.+(A), −(B)
D.ParasitismIV.+(A), +(B)
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: Mutualism benefits both species: +, + (A-IV). Commensalism benefits one and leaves the other unaffected: +, 0 (B-I). Amensalism harms one and leaves the other unaffected: −, 0 (C-II). Parasitism benefits the parasite and harms the host: +, − (D-III).
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
$\textbf{Statement I :}$ Gause’s ‘Competitive Exclusion Principle’ states that two closely related species competing for the same resources cannot co-exist indefinitely and competitively inferior one will be eliminated eventually.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$ In general, carnivores are more adversely affected by competition than herbivores.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true.
questions.sol:
Statement I is the correct statement of Gause’s competitive exclusion principle.
Statement II is false: in general, herbivores and plants are more adversely affected by competition than carnivores.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Match List I with List II :
List IList II
A.IronI.Synthesis of auxin
B.ZincII.Component of nitrate reductase
C.BoronIII.Activator of catalase
D.MolybdenumIV.Cell elongation and differentiation
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: Iron activates catalase (A-III). Zinc is needed for the synthesis of auxin (B-I). Boron is needed for cell elongation and cell differentiation, among other roles (C-IV). Molybdenum is a component of nitrate reductase and nitrogenase (D-II).
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Main steps in the formation of Recombinant DNA are given below. Arrange these steps in a correct sequence.
A. Insertion of recombinant DNA into the host cell.
B. Cutting of DNA at specific location by restriction enzyme.
C. Isolation of desired DNA fragment.
D. Amplification of gene of interest using PCR.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
NCERT lists the steps of recombinant DNA technology as isolation of DNA, cutting it at specific locations with restriction enzymes, amplification of the gene of interest by PCR, ligation into a vector and insertion of the recombinant DNA into the host: C, B, D, A (option 3).
If C is read as isolating the desired fragment after the DNA has been cut (separating it by gel electrophoresis and eluting it), the order becomes B, C, D, A (option 1). Both readings end with amplification and insertion, and NTA accepts both.
questions.subject: Botany
questions.note: NTA's final key accepts both option (1) and option (3). Statement C can mean isolating the DNA before cutting (C, B, D, A) or isolating the desired fragment after cutting (B, C, D, A).

questions.text:
Match List I with List II.
List IList II
A.VasectomyI.Oral method
B.Coitus interruptusII.Barrier method
C.Cervical capsIII.Surgical method
D.SaheliIV.Natural method
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: Vasectomy (cutting and tying the vas deferens) is a surgical method (A-III). Coitus interruptus (withdrawal) is a natural method (B-IV). Cervical caps are barriers that stop sperm reaching the uterus (C-II). Saheli is the once-a-week oral contraceptive pill developed at CDRI, Lucknow (D-I).
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
$\textbf{Statement I:}$ Vas deferens receives a duct from seminal vesicle and opens into urethra as the ejaculatory duct.
$\textbf{Statement II:}$ The cavity of the cervix is called cervical canal which along with vagina forms birth canal.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
Statement I incorrect but Statement II is true.
questions.sol:
Statement I is true: the vas deferens is joined by the duct of the seminal vesicle and continues into the urethra as the ejaculatory duct.
Statement II is true: the cavity of the cervix, the cervical canal, together with the vagina forms the birth canal.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: Eutrophication refers to increase in domestic sewage and waste water in lakes.
Biomagnification refers to increase in concentration of the toxicant at successive trophic levels.
Presence of large amount of nutrients in water restricts ‘Algal Bloom’
questions.sol:
Biomagnification is the rise in concentration of a toxicant (such as DDT or mercury) at each successive trophic level, because it is not broken down or excreted.
Eutrophication is the nutrient enrichment and natural ageing of a lake, not simply an increase in sewage; a large amount of nutrients causes algal blooms rather than restricting them; and algal blooms lower dissolved oxygen, which increases fish deaths.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: Which one of the following symbols represents mating between relatives in human pedigree analysis?
questions.sol: In pedigree charts a single horizontal line joins a male and a female in an ordinary mating, while a double line marks consanguineous mating (mating between relatives). Option (2) shows the double line. Option (3) is parents with an affected son and option (4) shows affected individuals.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: Which one of the following common sexually transmitted diseases is completely curable when detected early and treated properly?
questions.sol: Except for hepatitis-B, genital herpes and HIV infection, the common STIs are completely curable if detected early and treated properly. Gonorrhoea is a bacterial infection and is cured with antibiotics.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text:
Match List I with List II.
List IList II
A.HeroinI.Effect on cardiovascular system
B.MarijuanaII.Slow down body function
C.CocaineIII.Painkiller
D.MorphineIV.Interfere with transport of dopamine
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: Heroin is a depressant that slows down body functions (A-II). Cannabinoids such as marijuana act mainly on the cardiovascular system (B-I). Cocaine interferes with the transport of the neurotransmitter dopamine (C-IV). Morphine is a strong sedative and painkiller (D-III).
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text:
Match List I with List II.
List I
(Type of Joint)		List II
(Found between)
A.Cartilaginous JointI.Between flat skull bones
B.Ball and Socket JointII.Between adjacent vertebrae in vertebral column
C.Fibrous JointIII.Between carpal and metacarpal of thumb
D.Saddle JointIV.Between Humerus and Pectoral girdle
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: Cartilaginous joints join adjacent vertebrae (A-II). The ball and socket joint lies between the humerus and the pectoral girdle (B-IV). Fibrous joints join the flat skull bones (C-I). The saddle joint lies between the carpal and the metacarpal of the thumb (D-III).
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
$\textbf{Statement I:}$ A protein is imagined as a line, the left end represented by first amino acid (C-terminal) and the right end represented by last amino acid (N-terminal)
$\textbf{Statement II:}$ Adult human haemoglobin, consists of 4 subunits (two subunits of $\alpha$ type and two subunits of $\beta$ type.)
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
questions.sol:
Statement I is false: the first amino acid at the left end is the N-terminal amino acid and the last one at the right end is the C-terminal amino acid; the statement reverses them.
Statement II is true: adult haemoglobin has quaternary structure with two $\alpha$ and two $\beta$ subunits.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text:
Which of the following are NOT considered as the part of endomembrane system?
A. Mitochondria
B. Endoplasmic Reticulum
C. Chloroplasts
D. Golgi complex
E. Peroxisomes
Choose the $\textbf{most appropriate}$ answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: The endomembrane system is the ER, Golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuoles, whose functions are coordinated. Mitochondria, chloroplasts and peroxisomes are not part of it. So A, C and E only.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
$\textbf{Statement I:}$ RNA mutates at a faster rate.
$\textbf{Statement II:}$ Viruses having RNA genome and shorter life span mutate and evolve faster.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I false but Statement II is true.
questions.sol: Both are true. The 2'-OH group makes RNA reactive and less stable, so it mutates faster than DNA. As a result, viruses with an RNA genome and a short life span mutate and evolve faster.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as $\textbf{Assertion A}$ and the other is labelled as $\textbf{Reason R.}$
$\textbf{Assertion A:}$ Endometrium is necessary for implantation of blastocyst.
$\textbf{Reason R:}$ In the absence of fertilization, the corpus luteum degenerates that causes disintegration of endometrium.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.sol:
A is true: the blastocyst becomes embedded in the endometrium of the uterus.
R is true: without fertilisation the corpus luteum degenerates, progesterone falls and the endometrium breaks down (menstruation).
But R explains what happens when there is no pregnancy, not why the endometrium is needed for implantation, so R is not the correct explanation of A.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
$\textbf{Statement I:}$ Low temperature preserves the enzyme in a temporarily inactive state whereas high temperature destroys enzymatic activity because proteins are denatured by heat.
$\textbf{Statement II:}$ When the inhibitor closely resembles the substrate in its molecular structure and inhibits the activity of the enzyme, it is known as competitive inhibitor.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
questions.sol: Both statements are the standard NCERT descriptions: low temperature keeps an enzyme temporarily inactive while heat denatures it, and an inhibitor that resembles the substrate and competes for the active site is a competitive inhibitor (for example malonate with succinic dehydrogenase).

questions.sol: $\textit{Taenia}$ (a flatworm) excretes through flame cells (A-III). $\textit{Paramoecium}$ uses a contractile vacuole (B-II). In $\textit{Periplaneta}$ (cockroach) the uricose glands help in excretion (C-IV). $\textit{Pheretima}$ (earthworm) has nephridia (D-I).

questions.text: Which one of the following techniques does not serve the purpose of early diagnosis of a disease for its early treatment?
questions.sol: Conventional methods such as serum and urine analysis can detect a disease only after symptoms have appeared, when the pathogen numbers are high. Recombinant DNA technology, PCR and ELISA can detect a pathogen at very low concentration, so they allow early diagnosis.

A.A Leopard and a Lion in a forest/grasslandI.Competition
B.A Cuckoo laying egg in a Crow’s nestII.Brood parasitism
C.Fungi and root of a higher plant in MycorrtizaeIII.Mutualism
D.A cattle egret and a Cattle in a fieldIV.Commensalism
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: Two predators hunting the same prey compete (A-I). The cuckoo lays its eggs in the crow's nest so that the crow raises its young: brood parasitism (B-II). In mycorrhizae the fungus and the plant root both benefit: mutualism (C-III). The cattle egret feeds on insects disturbed by grazing cattle, which are unaffected: commensalism (D-IV).

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
$\textbf{Statement I:}$ Ligaments are dense irregular tissue.
$\textbf{Statement II:}$ Cartilage is dense regular tissue.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
questions.sol: Ligaments (and tendons) are dense regular connective tissue, with collagen fibres in parallel bundles, so Statement I is false. Cartilage is a specialised connective tissue, not dense regular tissue, so Statement II is false.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
$\textbf{Statement I:}$ In prokaryotes, the positively charged DNA is held with some negatively charged proteins in a region called nucleoid.
$\textbf{Statement II:}$ In eukaryotes, the negatively charged DNA is wrapped around the positively charged histone octamer to form nucleosome.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
Statement I incorrect but Statement II is true.
questions.sol:
Statement I is incorrect: DNA is negatively charged (phosphate groups), and in prokaryotes it is held with some positively charged proteins in the nucleoid.
Statement II is correct: negatively charged DNA wraps around the positively charged histone octamer to form a nucleosome.

B.IrisII.External layer of eye formed of dense connective tissue.
C.Blind spotIII.Point of greatest visual acuity or resolution.

questions.sol: The fovea, packed with cones, is the point of greatest visual acuity (A-III). The iris is the visible coloured part that controls the diameter of the pupil (B-I). At the blind spot the optic nerve leaves the eye and there are no photoreceptors (C-IV). The sclera is the outer layer of dense connective tissue (D-II).
