questions.text: Select the correct group/set of Australian Marsupials exhibiting adaptive radiation.
options: Mole, Flying squirrel, Tasmanian tiger cat
questions.sol: The numbat (banded anteater), spotted cuscus and flying phalanger are all Australian marsupials that radiated from a common ancestor. Each of the other options contains placental mammals (bobcat, mole, flying squirrel, lemur, anteater, wolf).

questions.text:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding female reproductive cycle?
A. In non-primate mammals cyclical changes during reproduction are called oestrus cycle.
B. First menstrual cycle begins at puberty and is called menopause.
C. Lack of menstruation may be indicative of pregnancy.
D. Cyclic menstruation extends between menarche and menopause.
Choose the $\textbf{most appropriate}$ answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: A, C and D are correct. B is wrong: the first menstruation at puberty is called menarche; menopause is when menstrual cycles stop at about 50 years of age.

questions.text: Vital capacity of lung is _______.
questions.sol: Vital capacity is the maximum volume of air breathed out after a forced inspiration: $\mathrm{VC} = \mathrm{ERV} + \mathrm{TV} + \mathrm{IRV}$. Adding RV gives the total lung capacity.

questions.sol: In the ECG the P peak shows depolarisation of the atria (A-III); the Q point marks the beginning of ventricular systole (B-I); the QRS complex shows depolarisation of the ventricles (C-IV); and the T peak shows their repolarisation (D-II).

$\textbf{Assertion A:}$ Amniocentesis for sex determination is one of the strategies of Reproductive and Child Health Care Programme.
$\textbf{Reason R:}$ Ban on amniocentesis checks increasing menace of female foeticide.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.sol:

R is true: the ban is meant to check the growing problem of female foeticide.

questions.sol: The cytoskeleton (microtubules, microfilaments and intermediate filaments) gives mechanical support, helps in motility and maintains the shape of the cell. Of the options given, motility is the function NCERT lists for it.

questions.text:
Given below are statements: one is labelled as $\textbf{Assertion A}$ and the other is labelled as $\textbf{Reason R.}$
$\textbf{Assertion A:}$ Nephrons are of two types: Cortical & Juxta medullary, based on their relative position in cortex and medulla.
$\textbf{Reason R:}$ Juxta medullary nephrons have short loop of Henle whereas, cortical nephrons have longer loop of Henle.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.sol:
A is true: nephrons are cortical or juxta medullary depending on how far the loop of Henle extends into the medulla.
R is false: it is the other way round. Cortical nephrons have a short loop of Henle that barely reaches the medulla, while juxta medullary nephrons have a very long loop that runs deep into it.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
$\textbf{Statement I:}$ Electrostatic precipitator is most widely used in thermal power plant.
$\textbf{Statement II:}$ Electrostatic precipitator in thermal power plant removes ionising radiations
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textit{most appropriate}$ answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.sol:
Statement I is correct: the electrostatic precipitator is the most widely used device for cleaning the exhaust of thermal power plants.
Statement II is incorrect: it removes particulate matter (about 99 per cent), not ionising radiation. Electrons released from the electrode wires charge the dust particles, which are then attracted to the collecting plates.

questions.text: Broad palm with single palm crease is visible in a person suffering from-
questions.sol: Down's syndrome (trisomy 21) is marked by short stature, a small round head, a furrowed tongue, a partly open mouth and a broad palm with a characteristic palm crease.

questions.text: Radial symmetry is NOT found in adults of phylum _______.
questions.sol: Coelenterates and ctenophores are radially symmetrical, and adult echinoderms are radially symmetrical (their larvae are bilateral). Hemichordates such as $\textit{Balanoglossus}$ are bilaterally symmetrical, so radial symmetry is not found in them.

questions.text: In which blood corpuscles, the HIV undergoes replication and produces progeny viruses?
questions.sol: HIV first enters macrophages, where its RNA is copied into viral DNA. It then enters helper T-lymphocytes ($\mathrm{T_H}$ cells), where it replicates and produces progeny viruses, steadily reducing the number of these cells.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a cloning vector?
questions.sol: BAC (bacterial artificial chromosome), YAC (yeast artificial chromosome) and the plasmid pBR322 are all cloning vectors. A probe is a labelled single-stranded piece of DNA or RNA used to find a complementary sequence, not a vector.

A.Logistic growthI.Unlimited resource availability condition
B.Exponential growthII.Limited resource availability condition
C.Expanding age pyramidIII.The percent individuals of pre-reproductive age is largest followed by reproductive and post reproductive age groups
D.Stable age pyramidIV.The percent individuals of pre-reproductives and reproductive age group are same
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: Logistic (sigmoid) growth happens when resources are limited (A-II); exponential growth when they are unlimited (B-I). An expanding (triangular) age pyramid has the largest share of pre-reproductive individuals (C-III). A stable (bell-shaped) pyramid has roughly equal pre-reproductive and reproductive groups (D-IV).

questions.text:
Select the correct statements with reference to chordates.
A. Presence of a mid-dorsal, solid and double nerve cord.
B. Presence of closed circulatory system.
C. Presence of paired pharyngeal gillslits.
D. Presence of dorsal heart
E. Triploblastic pseudocoelomate animals.
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: Chordates have a closed circulatory system (B) and paired pharyngeal gill slits (C). The nerve cord is dorsal, hollow and single (not solid and double), the heart is ventral, and chordates are triploblastic coelomates, so A, D and E are wrong. So B and C only.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: The parts of human brain that helps in regulation of sexual behaviour, expression of excitement, pleasure, rage, fear etc. are :
questions.sol: The limbic system (amygdala, hippocampus and related structures) together with the hypothalamus regulates sexual behaviour and the expression of emotions such as excitement, pleasure, rage and fear, as well as motivation.

questions.text: The unique mammalian characteristics are:
options: hairs, tympanic membrane and mammary glands
pinna, monocondylic skull and mammary glands
questions.sol: The most distinctive features of mammals are mammary glands, hair on the skin and external ears (pinnae). A tympanic membrane is also found in amphibians, reptiles and birds; mammals have direct development and a dicondylic skull.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text:
Which of the following are NOT under the control of thyroid hormone?
A. Maintenance of water and electrolyte balance
B. Regulation of basal metabolic rate
C. Normal rhythm of sleep-wake cycle
D. Development of immune system
E. Support the process of R.B.Cs formation
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: NCERT lists regulation of the basal metabolic rate, support for red blood cell formation and maintenance of water and electrolyte balance as functions of the thyroid hormones. The sleep-wake rhythm is controlled by melatonin (pineal gland) and the development of the immune system by thymosins (thymus). So C and D only.

questions.text:
Select the correct statements.
A. Tetrad formation is seen during Leptotene.
B. During Anaphase, the centromeres split and chromatids separate.
C. Terminalization takes place during Pachytene.
D. Nucleolus, Golgi complex and ER are reformed during Telophase.
E. Crossing over takes place between sister chromatids of homologous chromosome.
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: B and D are correct. A is wrong: tetrads (bivalents) become visible in pachytene, after synapsis in zygotene. C is wrong: terminalisation of chiasmata happens in diakinesis. E is wrong: crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes.

questions.text: Which of the following is characteristic feature of cockroach regarding sexual dimorphism ?
options: Dark brown body colour and anal cerci
questions.sol: Both sexes of cockroach have a brown body, sclerites and a pair of anal cerci. Only the male has a pair of short, thread-like anal styles on the 9th sternum, so anal styles show sexual dimorphism.

questions.text: Which one of the following is the sequence on corresponding coding strand, if the sequence on mRNA formed is as follows 5’ AUCGAUCGAUCGAUCGAUCGAUCG AUCG 3’?
questions.sol: The coding strand has the same sequence and the same 5'$\to$3' polarity as the mRNA, except that it has T in place of U. So it is 5' ATCGATCG...ATCG 3'. Options (1) and (2) contain U, so they cannot be DNA.

In cockroach, excretion is brought about by-
A. Phallic gland
B. Urecose gland
C. Nephrocytes
D. Fat body
E. Collaterial glands
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: Excretion in the cockroach is mainly by Malpighian tubules, helped by the fat body, nephrocytes and uricose glands. The phallic gland (male) and the collaterial glands (female) are reproductive glands. So B, C and D only.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
$\textbf{Statement I:}$ During $\mathrm{G_0}$ phase of cell cycle, the cell is metabolically inactive.
$\textbf{Statement II:}$ The centrosome undergoes duplication during S phase of interphase.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textit{most appropriate}$ answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.sol:
Statement I is incorrect: cells in the quiescent $\mathrm{G_0}$ stage remain metabolically active but do not proliferate.
Statement II is correct: in animal cells the centriole (centrosome) duplicates in the cytoplasm during the S phase.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: Which one of the following is NOT an advantage of inbreeding?
options: It exposes harmful recessive genes that are eliminated by selection.
Elimination of less desirable genes and accumulation of superior genes takes place due to it.
It decreases the productivity of inbred population, after continuous inbreeding.
questions.sol: Continued inbreeding reduces fertility and productivity (inbreeding depression), which is a drawback, not an advantage. Inbreeding increases homozygosity, exposes harmful recessive genes so that they can be removed by selection, and helps accumulate superior genes.
questions.subject: Zoology
questions.note: Option (1) is also not an advantage, since inbreeding increases homozygosity rather than decreasing it; the NTA key gives only option (4), the disadvantage (inbreeding depression).

questions.text:
Which of the following statements are correct?
A. An excessive loss of body fluid from the body switches off osmoreceptors.
B. ADH facilitates water reabsorption to prevent diuresis.
C. ANF causes vasodilation.
D. ADH causes increase in blood pressure.
E. ADH is responsible for decrease in GFR.
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: B, C and D are correct. A is wrong: excessive loss of body fluid activates the osmoreceptors, which trigger ADH release. E is wrong: by constricting blood vessels ADH raises blood pressure, which can increase glomerular blood flow and hence the GFR.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding skeletal muscle?
A. Muscle bundles are held together by collagenous connective tissue layer called fascicle.
B. Sarcoplasmic reticulum of muscle fibre is a store house of calcium ions.
C. Striated appearance of skeletal muscle fibre is due to distribution pattern of actin and myosin proteins.
D. M line is considered as functional unit of contraction called sarcomere.
Choose the $\textit{most appropriate}$ answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: B and C are correct. A is wrong: the muscle bundles (fascicles) are held together by a collagenous connective tissue layer called fascia. D is wrong: the sarcomere, the functional unit of contraction, is the portion of a myofibril between two successive Z lines; the M line is the thin membrane at the centre of the A band.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text:
Which of the following statements are correct ?
A. Basophils are most abundant cells of the total WBCs
B. Basophils secrete histamine, serotonin and heparin
C. Basophils are involved in inflammatory response
D. Basophils have kidney shaped nucleus
E. Basophils are agranulocytes
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: Basophils secrete histamine, serotonin and heparin and take part in inflammatory reactions, so B and C are correct. They are the least numerous WBCs (0.5–1 per cent), they are granulocytes, and the kidney-shaped nucleus belongs to monocytes.
